title: Kira's quantization & prompt scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Sprint focus: reduce per-token cost for 8k context chat workloads without degrading helpfulness. Try int8-ish quant profiles + KV-cache heuristics. Low-risk eval on small internal dataset first.
- Platform: Redwood Dedicated test pool (p4d-reserved-sim), model variant: rw-bert-chat-13b (fp16 baseline), candidate: rw-bert-chat-13b-llm-int8 (dynamic quant).

Running notes / things I did (rough):
- 2026-03-09: baseline microbench with fp16, seq_len=2048, batch=8, single stream sim. Tokens/sec ~ 320 (median).
- 2026-03-10: enabled dynamic int8 quant using quant-profile v3 (try A/B). Observed 1.9x speedup throughput but occasional failure on long attention span >6k (OOM-ish).
- 2026-03-11: patched tokenizer padding in PR (see linked PR) to avoid degenerate long padding sequences that blow memory in quant path.
- 2026-03-12: ran KV-cache prefix reuse test (cache warmup enabled). Notice: int8 path has ~10% higher latency p95 on cold requests vs fp16, likely due to extra dequant/decompress step on cache hits.

Hypotheses (to verify):
- H1: Int8 dynamic quant introduces extra dequant overhead on cached KV blocks because we decompress per-block instead of keeping compressed in GPU-readable format. Should be possible to stash compressed blocks in scratchpad memory.
- H2: The OOM on long attention is due to our intermediate accumulate buffers using fp32 in the int8 codepath; changing accumulation to bf16 might reduce peak mem.
- H3: Prompt engineering (shorter system prompt + explicit context trimming) yields comparable quality to full prompt while reducing effective seq_len and enabling smaller batch sizes -> cost win.

Prompt set (quick):
- sys: "You are a concise assistant. Provide a short answer, then one-line explanation."
- user1: "Summarize the following meeting notes into 3 bullets: [LONG TEXT]"
- user2: "Rewrite this product spec into a launch checklist."
- note: keep template tokens ~30, avoid long preambles for microbench fairness.

Microbench log snippet (hand-collected):
- fp16 baseline (batch=8, seq=2048): median 320 tok/s, p95 latency 210ms per chunk
- int8 v3 (batch=8, seq=2048): median 610 tok/s, p95 latency 240ms per chunk (cold) / 215ms (warm)
- int8 w/kv-warm (batch=8, seq=2048): median 590 tok/s, p95 latency 230ms
- notes: throughput gains look good but p95 regression on cold path needs improvement; quality eval TBD.

Quality eval plan (short):
- Use 200-item eval set from conv-quality-2026 (mix of summarization, instruction-following).
- Metrics: exact match for extractive, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, and human-rated helpfulness (1-5) for instruction tasks. 20-sample human eval subset.
- Compare: fp16 baseline vs int8-v3 vs int8-v3 + prompt-trim.

Open issues / TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] INF-5621: Investigate OOM on long-attn for int8 path (assigned to Samir).
- [ ] Add compressed-KV prototype: keep compressed tensors on GPU and decompress only when necessary (prototype in local branch kira/int8-kv-cache).
- [ ] Run 200-item eval for quality: schedule on Dedicated test pool (need 4h slot).
- [ ] Add automated microbench harness to measure cold vs warm p95 separately.
- [ ] Try bf16 accumulation in quant kernel (low-risk, measure mem footprint).
- [ ] Document prompt-trim recipes in confluence page (TODO: expand examples).

Quick commands / snippets: (for my future self)
- run microbench: python infra/bench/run_microbench.py --model rw-bert-chat-13b --quant-profile v3 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --pool dedicated-test
- run eval: python evals/run_eval.py --set conv-quality-2026 --model candidate --out /tmp/eval_kira.json
- snapshot logs: rcli fetch-logs --job-id <job> --dest /tmp/logs; tar czf /tmp/kira-logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tgz /tmp/logs

Random notes to self (messy):
- If compressed KV reduces memory copy on cache-hits we might avoid dequant at every step. Check GPU memcpy hotspots in nvprof logs.
- Consider a hybrid: store recent keys as bf16 (cheap) and less-recent compressed int8 blocks on device.
- Talk to infra about adding a p4d debug instance with nvlink tracing enabled.
- Remind Maya to run the human eval recruitment script (she owns the 20-sample human set).

Meeting follow-ups / calls:
- 2026-03-13 10:00 sync with Samir + Maya (15m): status on INF-5621 + plan for eval run.
- Agenda: results so far, plan for compressed-KV prototype, who will run the 4h eval slot.

End-of-day: prioritize compressed-KV prototype (low-effort patch in runtime) and schedule eval run. Keep notes minimal here; expand in confluence when results are stable.

-- Kira
